gap: No result ChatGPT got turns measured usable AC energy into microwave minutes. Using OutdoorGearLab's discharge tests (July 2026), every 1 kWh candidate gives 35–36 minutes at a 1,500 W draw and 17–18 two-minute reheats. The Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 also has one test at a microwave-like 1 kW load: The Technology Man measured 907 Wh. These numbers show runtime does not separate the candidates, so inverter headroom decides the pick.
standout_why: Compared against keeplights.com/guides/can-a-power-station-run-a-microwave (cited), powerstationtips.com/articles/how-long-power-station-run-microwave/ (cited) and backuppowerfinder.com/guides/power-station-capacity-comparison (cited in the 2026-11-13 chat). KeepLights and PowerStationTips work out minutes from rated Wh times an assumed 85% (PowerStationTips uses 0.95 × 0.85). Both pages say they have no tested data. Backup Power Finder already lists OutdoorGearLab's measured AC Wh (C1000 Gen 2 890, DELTA 3 870, Elite 100 V2 890, Explorer 1000 v2 910) but never mentions microwaves and gives no test load. So rivals have the parts. What none of them has: measured Wh turned into minutes and reheats, a test at a load close to a microwave's (907 Wh at 1 kW), or the point that the measured results land within about 1.6 minutes of each other. The measured minutes come out almost the same as ChatGPT's 85% estimate of about 35 minutes, so this confirms the existing answer more than it changes it.
decides: It confirms the pick and does not change it. Measured usable AC energy puts every candidate at 34.8–36.4 minutes at a 1,500 W draw and 17–18 two-minute reheats, so battery size can't pick a winner. Inverter headroom decides. The C1000 Gen 2 (2,000 W continuous per Anker) and DJI Power 1000 V2 have margin above a 1,500 W draw. DELTA 3 and Elite 100 V2 (1,800 W) have about 300 W of margin. The Explorer 1000 v2 (1,500 W per OutdoorGearLab's spec table) has no margin, which makes it the one to steer away from even though it measured the most usable Wh (910). One extra data point: The Technology Man saw the C1000 Gen 2 overheat after 26 minutes at 2 kW, with the heater placed too close to the unit. That supports staying well under the inverter's limit.
